Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right apical cavitary lesion containing a rounded mass with a surrounding lucency (air crescent sign), which is the classic radiographic appearance of an aspergilloma (fungus ball). This finding is consistent with patients who have pre-existing lung cavities, such as those from prior tuberculosis or bullous disease associated with connective tissue disorders like Marfan syndrome.
